title: Forgiveness

verse.english: But with you there is forgiveness, so that we can, with reverence, serve you.

readings.author: Rashi
readings.heading: Turn toward God
readings.text: Rashi reads this as forgiveness that God has not delegated to an angel. The prayer directs us toward God, where divine pardon is sought.

readings.author: Ibn Ezra
readings.heading: Hope can spread
readings.text: When others hear that a sin has been forgiven, they may turn back too. One person’s forgiveness can encourage another person to change.

readings.author: Meiri
readings.heading: A reason to try
readings.text: If repentance could never help, a person might give up after doing wrong. The promise of forgiveness keeps failure from becoming a reason for despair.

readings.author: Malbim
readings.heading: Mercy inspires awe
readings.text: A ruler may use punishment to make people afraid. Malbim sees God’s greatness revealed in forgiveness itself. Mercy can awaken reverence.

questions: Why might being forgiven deepen reverence?
Whose example has helped you believe that change is possible?
Does forgiveness make you more accountable, or less? Why?

further_reading.author: Rabbi Jonathan Sacks
further_reading.title: The Birth of Forgiveness
further_reading.note: Joseph, Judah, and the possibility of change.
